answer: Every new agent must dock at one public jetty: before it can transact, it posts a small refundable stake plus a signed record of one real completed job. The shared ledger acts as a mirror, reflecting each agent's full history so anyone can check whether its reputation was earned or freshly invented. A prism check then splits that history into separate facets — stake age, completed jobs, peer ratings — and a fake identity fails because it cannot fabricate all three at once; spinning up a thousand convincing histories costs a thousand stakes and a thousand real jobs.
